title: Align payable guidance and historical evidence with current approval state
trigger: Actual first accountant browser review completed the rehearsal with 17/20 and identified five clarity findings, controller-mapped as KONTOR-ACCOUNTANT-R1-01 through 05. UX /root/build_ux proposed bounded copy changes, PM /root/build_pm accepted product priority, SDE /root/build_sde confirmed feasible original implementation, and PM accepted after one engineering round. The review used fresh context but non-isolated tools; this is controller-attested evidence, not an isolated browser-worker receipt.
productRationale: Contradictory approval instructions can cause an accountant to repeat completed work or doubt payment readiness. Correcting current-state instructions is the principal priority; adjacent role guidance, explicit historical approval expiry and JSON export labeling remove related inference without expanding the product. The successful rehearsal and comprehension support a bounded improvement, not a broader workflow redesign or a production accountant-acceptance claim.
engineeringDecision: Accept the original UX proposal and feasible SDE implementation with no counterproposal or unresolved objection. Existing state supports distinct current required approvers, authoritative status, named people and roles, event revisions and one credit-note reference. Derive presentation only: 0/2 and 1/2 instructions name remaining work; 2/2 plus approved status names the payment operator and confirms readiness. Paid and pending/unknown states take precedence. Display historical expiry only with explicit approval-revision, credit-event revision and credit-reference linkage; omit ambiguous annotations. Preserve stored evidence and exported data. Change only src/App.tsx and src/styles.css if necessary.
constraints: This is improvement cycle 1 of at most two authorized cycles within the shared $10 additional-spend ceiling. Parent remains sole control-plane writer and will persist the decision before implementation. approvedImplementationTasks remains empty until canonical task assignment.

Presentation-only scope: src/App.tsx and src/styles.css if needed. Do not change APIs, program, server, permissions, approval operations, credit operations, settlement operations or immutable/exported evidence.

Derive approval counts from distinct required identities for the current revision. At original and revised 0/2 or 1/2, show only remaining work. At 2/2 plus authoritative approved status, show completed approval and named executor guidance. Never retain an approval imperative after both current approvals or claim readiness during paid/pending/unknown states.
Preserve reviewer credit access before payment. Beside a non-reviewer disabled credit control, name the authorized reviewer and role in readable non-hover text at desktop and 390 px.

Historical approval display includes invoice version and expiry after the actual credit reference only when the event-revision linkage establishes it. Retain original title/detail, state object and downloaded JSON. The one-credit model supports this logic; do not generalize to arbitrary future histories or infer expiry from amount difference. Omit absent or ambiguous linkage.
Rename the existing control Export evidence (JSON). Printable accounting summaries, new formats and certification claims remain deferred.

Accept all UX proposal acceptance criteria. Run existing typecheck and production build, check scope/data preservation, and conduct fresh-context accountant regression across original/revised 0/2, 1/2 and 2/2 guidance, role hint, historical/current evidence, export label and one 800 Test USD completion at desktop and 390 px.
Retain visible amount and next action at the agreed desktop viewport despite added helper text. Keep readable narrow layouts, accessible statuses and existing recovery behavior.

Preserve rehearsal versus actual devnet distinctions. Parent-reported successful live proofs of both orderings are independent source-aware evidence and do not change the first accountant review's rehearsal-only scope. The follow-up browser review is non-isolated usability evidence, not proof of blockchain enforcement, production accounting acceptance or genuinely blind evaluation.
rejectedAlternatives: Leave completed-approval instructions unchanged because the task succeeded: contradicts the core readiness story and causes avoidable doubt.
Add printable evidence now: useful later, but expands a bounded copy correction into a new output-format feature.
Rewrite original history or exported evidence to remove ambiguity: derived display annotations preserve the immutable original record.
Infer historical expiry from amount differences or count raw approval entries: can produce incorrect status; use exact revision/reference linkage and distinct required approvers.
Broader workflow or authorization changes: unsupported by these observed findings and unnecessary for this improvement.
